evidence: Photoluminescence measurements at 15 and 77 K were performed to characterize the optical properties of AlGaAs materials and AlGaAs/GaAs quantum wells. Room temperature Hall measurement was used to evaluate carrier concentrations. The ALE process has an improvement in the optical properties that can be related to the enhancement in the surface migration of column III adsorbed atoms. The 4 K photoluminescence displayed well resolved bound exciton transitions characteristic of high purity GaAs. The growth of AsGaAs was done in a low pressure reactor with a resistive heated molybdenum susceptor. A set of three AlGaAs/GaAs quantum wells were grown by ALE at 680°C. The 15 K photoluminescence spectrum for Al0.3Ga0.7As/GaAs multiple quantum wells grown by ALE technique. The 77 K PL emission wavelength distribution of a Al0.3Ga0.7As/GaAs single quantum well grown at 680°C solely by ALE technique. The 4 K photoluminescence spectrum of high purity GaAs grown by ALE at 600°C. The excitonic region of this spectra is dominated by excitons bound to neutral donors. The V/Ill ratio was 130. The total hydrogen was 12 SLM and was evenly divided between the background flow in the reactor and the flow through the injection manifolds of the reagents and hydrogen purge jets.
